questions.prompt: Which first-generation cephalosporin is used as a standard surgical prophylaxis to prevent *Staphylococcus aureus* wound infections by inhibiting peptidoglycan cross-linking?

A 28-year-old male presents with a single, painless ulcer on his penis that appeared one week ago. Physical examination reveals a clean-based, indurated ulcer and bilateral, non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Darkfield microscopic examination of the lesion exudate demonstrates motile, tightly coiled spirochetes. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment of choice for this patient?

A 6-year-old child is diagnosed with a tick-borne infection. Which of the following antibiotic classes should be avoided in this patient due to the risk of permanent tooth discoloration and inhibition of bone growth?
Which bactericidal agent requires an oxygen-dependent transporter to enter the cell and exerts its effect by binding irreversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit, causing mRNA misreading?

A 65-year-old patient presents with a productive cough, and sputum Gram stain reveals Gram-positive, lancet-shaped diplococci. Which of the following is the most appropriate empirical treatment if high-level penicillin resistance via altered penicillin-binding proteins is suspected?

A patient presents with a few hairless, hypopigmented skin plaques on his trunk that have a complete loss of sensation. Physical examination also reveals visible enlargement of the ulnar and peroneal nerves. A skin biopsy confirms the presence of acid-fast bacilli. He received the appropriate treatment for this condition. Ten days later, he presents with significant fatigue, jaundice, and dark-coloured urine. Laboratory evaluation reveals evidence of acute hemolytic anemia. Which of the following drugs is most likely to be the cause of this patient's new symptoms?

A patient being treated for a vaginal infection develops severe flushing, tachycardia, and hypotension after consuming a glass of wine. Which of the following drugs is most likely responsible for this reaction?
Which of the following describes the molecular mechanism by which ciprofloxacin inhibits bacterial DNA synthesis?
options: Binding to the 30S ribosomal subunit to prevent initiation
Inhibition of the beta-subunit of RNA polymerase
Inhibition of DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV

questions.prompt: A patient with cystic fibrosis develops a pulmonary infection with *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*. Which of the following drugs treats this infection by disrupting bacterial cell wall synthesis?
For which patient population or clinical scenario is the use of bacteriostatic agents generally discouraged in favor of bactericidal therapy?
options: Young, sexually active women with simple cystitis
A patient with a secondary pharyngitis during infectious mononucleosis
Pediatric patients with minor respiratory tract infections
An immunocompromised host or a patient with a life-threatening infection
A patient with a localized, uncomplicated skin infection
